sources.supportedQualification: Crisp sets allow multiple members with binary grades; fuzzy membership is degree of belonging. Min/max are selectable operators, not the only possible fuzzy conjunction/disjunction. Antecedents and consequents have different roles.

Mamdani rule outputs are fuzzy sets aggregated then defuzzified. Singleton weighted methods differ from area geometry. This does not label the custom max-per-consequent reconstruction as standard Sugeno.
Centroid/defuzz routines consume an output universe and membership function; clipping/aggregation choices must be specified.
Gaussian, triangular, trapezoidal and S/Z membership APIs provide parameterized shapes; docs identify themselves asv0.3, not assumed current runtime.

Explicit antecedent/consequent universes, membership definitions, rule objects and simulation inputs are necessary to reproduce an implementation. This example is not the lecture cooling/robot program.
